raised.claim: The model-authored issue body is placed before the trusted scope block, so an earlier `triage-scope` fence in that body still hijacks the next run's parse.
raised.why_it_breaks: A new_issue body containing ```triage-scope followed by valid JSON such as {"beer_ids":[999],"where":[]} is saved ahead of the rendered block; parseScopeBlock takes the first match, so subsequent attachments are checked against scope 999 rather than the structured scope that was validated and planned.

raised.claim: Adding any enumerated beer_id makes a whole-class `where` legal, bypassing guard 1.
raised.why_it_breaks: The natural proposal {beer_ids:[1], where:[{col:'review_class',op:'=',value:'matcher_bug'}]} is accepted; row 1 passes through the cohort and every future matcher_bug row outside the cohort passes through the `where`, recreating the whole-class magnet the guard is meant to reject.

raised.claim: Verdicts routed to a proposed new issue are never checked against that issue's scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: A verdict for a row with candidates_count=0 can reference a new issue scoped candidates_count>0; the issue is created and the row is reviewed against it even though the same attachment to an existing issue would be rejected as a scope violation.

raised.claim: The saturation check uses a fixed pre-run count and does not account for verdicts accepted earlier in the same plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue has 11 post-creation rows and the model returns 20 otherwise-valid verdicts for it, all 20 pass because postCreationRows remains 11 for every iteration, producing 31 rows despite MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE being 12.

raised.quote:
const probe = probes.get(verdict.beer_id);
      const proved = probe?.brewery === '' || probe?.name === '';
raised.claim: One empty probe is treated as proof of absence even when the other probe returned the beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: For {brewery:'', name:'Some Beer — Brewery'}, the guard accepts not_on_untappd even though the name probe returned a hit; under the prompt's own different-brewery case this is a brewery-label/matcher problem, yet the row receives the terminal absence classification.

raised.claim: Guard diagnostics are omitted precisely when every row has a verdict but guards reject some or all of those verdicts.
raised.why_it_breaks: A model that returns one illegal-scope proposal per row has covered===orphans.length while plan.skipped and guardHits.illegal_scope are nonzero; no shortfall warning is emitted, so the recurring guard loop the new counter is intended to expose remains invisible in that log.

raised.claim: not_on_untappd verdicts degraded to matcher_bug by guard 3 are reported as wontfix in the run outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: An unprobed absence verdict is pushed into plan.quiet with review_class matcher_bug; the loop's else branch then increments wontfix, so the persisted digest claims a wontfix decision that was never made.

raised.quote:
reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Re-opening a review on the 0↔>0 candidate boundary clears the other review fields but leaves the new issue_number link stale.
raised.why_it_breaks: After a row reviewed against #408 fails again with candidates_count crossing the boundary, review_class, review_note, and reviewed_at become NULL while issue_number remains 408; the untriaged row therefore still claims an attachment to #408, corrupting the authoritative row-to-issue audit link introduced by v23.

raised.claim: Lexicographically comparing GitHub's second-precision creation timestamp with JavaScript's millisecond review timestamps can omit rows reviewed in the creation second.
raised.why_it_breaks: For createdAt 2026-08-14T06:00:00Z and reviewed_at 2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z, the review is later chronologically but SQLite compares '.' with 'Z' and evaluates reviewed_at > createdAt as false, undercounting post-creation rows and weakening saturation.
